baseline_models.focus_anchor: The interrogative "ألم يروا", the quantity "كم", and the sequence "أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون ... لا يرجعون".
baseline_models.mechanism: The question makes the disappearance of many earlier, time-bound cohorts into apprehensible evidence: they preceded the hearers, fell into destruction, and cannot resume their former movement toward the present.

activation_trace.role: Seeing by eye or insight makes the opening a demand to apprehend evidence.
Falling into ruin and disappearance supplies the terminal event applied to the cohorts.
Temporal precedence places the destroyed cohorts earlier on the hearers' own timeline.
People joined within one time supplies the unit repeatedly counted by "كم".
Return to a former state or place supplies the movement explicitly denied.

changed_reading.before: Earlier peoples were destroyed and do not come back.
changed_reading.after: The hearers are pressed to recognize a repeated historical fact: whole time-bound cohorts disappear in a one-way sequence, and the present cohort stands where they can no longer stand.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The bound cohort-image in "القرون" and the directional phrase "إليهم لا يرجعون".
baseline_models.mechanism: A generation is not merely a plurality but a company joined in one time. Its nonreturn therefore severs a social and historical link: predecessors cannot rejoin, answer, correct, or reinforce the living group addressed by "إليهم".

activation_trace.role: Binding one thing to another turns a generation into an internally joined company.
Companionship sharpens the social body whose continuity is broken.
Denied return prevents that former company from re-entering the present relation.

changed_reading.before: The dead simply fail to return.
changed_reading.after: Destruction breaks the intergenerational relay: the living cannot expect vanished cohorts to come back into their community and repair what history has closed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah repeatedly places signs before the audience while describing barriers, failed sight, and active turning-away. The focus question therefore diagnoses a failed response to available evidence, not a lack of evidence.

activation_trace.role: The alerting and interrogative branch makes "ألم يروا" a pointed diagnostic challenge.
Barriers closing the gaps in front and behind model an enclosed field of perception.
Heart-insight extends the stated failure to see beyond missing ocular contact.
Turning one's side away supplies an active refusal mechanism when signs arrive.
A second alerting sight-question applies the same examination to familiar created goods.
A third sight-question turns the examination inward to the human's own origin.

structural_cues: 36:9 closes its barrier scene with "فهم لا يبصرون", while 36:46 says each sign meets "معرضين".
The openings of 36:31, 36:71, and 36:77 repeat the same negative sight-question across history, provision, and human origin.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies visible signs, blocked sight, turning-away, and repeated interrogatives; I infer that the focus failure is culpable or conditioned non-recognition rather than evidentiary scarcity. A live alternative is a narrower demand for ordinary historical observation.

changed_reading.before: The audience is asked whether it knows what happened to earlier peoples.
changed_reading.after: The audience's inability or refusal to recognize an abundant historical sign is itself under examination; "seeing" names a moral-intellectual response to evidence already before them.

context_deltas.mechanism: The town narrative gives one worked instance of the focus pattern: a message is delivered and rejected, one cry arrests the community's life, and the following lament generalizes mockery of messengers before "كم" generalizes destruction across many cohorts.

activation_trace.role: Messenger and message initiate the town's test before its destruction.
The terrifying single cry supplies the compact destructive event.
Life becoming still after movement renders communal extinction as sudden cessation.
The singular town episode expands into the recurring arrival of messengers to servants.
Repeated mockery supplies the social response linking the exemplar to the general lament.
The focus destruction gathers the exemplar's sudden stilling into a repeated historical class.

structural_cues: 36:13-29 moves from the arrival of messengers to one cry and a wholly stilled community.
36:30 shifts from that episode to a general lament over mocked messengers, and 36:31 immediately asks how many cohorts were destroyed.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the narrative sequence and its immediate generalizing transitions; I infer a recurring rejection-to-destruction mechanism behind the focus count. The live alternative is that the town is illustrative without making messenger mockery the cause of every destruction counted.

changed_reading.before: The verse cites an unspecified number of destroyed predecessors.
changed_reading.after: The verse converts the just-told town into one case within a recurrent social mechanism: communities meet warning with mockery until active communal life is abruptly stilled.

context_deltas.mechanism: Recorded traces keep destroyed communities evidentially present, while the surah repeatedly models life emerging from death and origination answering decay. Nonreturn to the present audience is therefore distinguished from absolute nonexistence or incapacity for re-creation.

activation_trace.role: Reflective judgment lets remaining effects make an absent cohort intellectually visible.
Ruin and disappearance name the historical loss that requires qualification.
The denied return is read as a specified movement toward "them", not every possible restoration.
A remaining mark that indicates what was makes vanished agents available through their آثار.
Earth restored to life by growth supplies a visible material analogy for reversal of death.
Decayed remains state the strongest material form of the objection to renewed life.
Bringing a thing into being supplies the answer from first origination to later decay.

structural_cues: 36:12 joins reviving the dead with writing what people sent ahead and their آثار before the town narrative begins.
After the focus, 36:33 revives dead earth, and 36:78-79 answers decayed bones by appeal to their first origination.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies persistent traces and several re-creation mechanisms; I infer that 36:31 denies historical-social return to the hearers rather than metaphysical restoration. A live alternative keeps the focus sentence strictly within worldly history without importing its later resurrection contrast.

changed_reading.before: Destruction and nonreturn amount to final disappearance.
changed_reading.after: Destroyed cohorts are absent as living interlocutors but remain legible through آثار, and their failure to return to the present does not bar divine re-creation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated directional constructions separate two destinations. The destroyed do not return "to them", and those overtaken by the cry do not return "to their people"; nevertheless humans are raised, gathered, made present "with Us", and returned "to Him".

activation_trace.role: The basic return movement is denied specifically along the direction marked by "إليهم".
Return remains affirmed when its destination is the Creator in "وإليه ترجعون".
Gathering dispersed persons reverses historical separation without restoring the old society.
Presence and nearness supply the new endpoint expressed by "لدينا".
Failure to return to one's people repeats the worldly and relational limit of return.
Arousing the still from rest supplies the transition from nonreturn to resurrection.
The dispersed become one gathered total after the second cry.
Their being made present with Us fixes the eschatological destination.
The surah's closing return to Him confirms return while changing its destination.

structural_cues: The focus says "إليهم لا يرجعون"; 36:22 and 36:83 say "وإليه ترجعون".
36:50 denies return "إلى أهلهم", then 36:51-53 moves through graves, raising, gathering, and presence "لدينا".
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies contrasting prepositional destinations and a nonreturn-to-kin followed by raising and assembly; I infer a two-destination topology, worldly return being closed while return to God remains. A live alternative treats each phrase locally without making the destination contrast a designed mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The destroyed never return in any sense.
changed_reading.after: They cannot return into the human community or historical moment they left, but that closed route is contrasted with another route: raising, gathering, and return to God.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This activation is surprising because it uses the packet's form-distant ر و ي mapping for the focus root rather than the direct sight mapping. It remains anchored in "يروا" and gains contextual support from the surah's self-description as recitation and its presented example; downstream prose should mark narrated or recited seeing as a possible medium of evidence, not as the lexical default.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus verb "يروا" as resolved not only to direct ر ء ي but also to the packet's ر و ي inventory.

activation_trace.role: Transmission of report or verse offers a form-distant medium through which absent history can be made present.
A formally presented example turns the town account into evidence supplied to the audience.
Reading and recitation identify the surah's own channel for transmitting that evidence.

changed_reading.before: Seeing earlier destruction requires direct observation or reflection on visible remains.
changed_reading.after: The recited report and its presented example may themselves function as the means by which vanished generations are made available to "seeing".

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain temporal analogy, not a claim that generations literally are celestial orbits. It remains anchored in the focus branches for time-bound cohorts, precedence, and denied return, while nearby measured recurrence, orbit, and life reversal supply the contrast. Downstream prose should qualify it as a possible whole-surah pattern: cosmic cycles return, but historical cohorts do not.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: "قبلهم من القرون" orders time-bound cohorts, while "لا يرجعون" denies their recurrence.

activation_trace.role: Precedence orders one cohort before another on a temporal line.
A people joined within one time supplies the discrete temporal cohort.
Denied return gives human succession its one-way direction.
The moon's return after departure supplies explicit recurrence within a measured cycle.
Counted time and its recurrence preserve the split root's temporal branch in the same cycle.
Circular motion supplies the contrasting domain in which ordered return is normal.
A life extended through time locates the human trajectory inside a finite span.
Being turned upside down supplies aging's reversal without restoring an earlier cohort.

changed_reading.before: Generations merely occur earlier and then disappear.
changed_reading.after: The focus may contrast two temporal regimes: creation displays measured recurrence, but each human cohort is bound to its time and cannot orbit back into history.

strongest_changes: The repeated sight-questions and scenes of blocked or refused perception turn "ألم يروا" into a diagnosis of non-recognition.
The town's messenger rejection, single cry, and stilling become one exemplar generalized by the focus count of destroyed cohorts.
Recorded آثار and repeated re-creation mechanisms separate nonreturn to the living from absolute nonexistence.
The contrast among "إليهم", "إلى أهلهم", "لدينا", and "إليه" distinguishes closed historical return from resurrection and return to God.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet exposed a precise destination contrast around رجع and placed the focus between a completed destruction narrative and immediate universal assembly, while later revival arguments prevented "لا يرجعون" from being flattened into absolute nonreturn.
remaining_uncertainties: The two-destination model depends on treating the pronoun and prepositional contrasts as a deliberate surah-wide mechanism rather than only local syntax.
The rejection-to-destruction mechanism is strongly sequenced here but need not describe the cause of every cohort counted by "كم".
Recited seeing and the contrast between cohort time and cosmic cycles remain explicitly exploratory cross-branch activations.
